options: The surrounding situation — a row, a set of active filters, or both — a formula is evaluated within
A setting in Power Query
The table a measure's home is set to
A type of DAX function
questions.explain: Context is the environment a formula runs in — which row, which filters — and it's the concept nearly every advanced DAX function exists to read or modify.

questions.q: What is row context most naturally associated with?
options: Only DirectQuery data sources
Calculated columns, which are evaluated once per row
Slicers and report-level filters
The CALCULATE function specifically
questions.explain: Row context is 'the current row' — it's the default evaluation environment for a calculated column, which computes a value for every row automatically.

questions.q: In 'Store Sales = CALCULATE([Total Sales], Channel[ChannelName] = "Store")', what does the filter argument represent?
options: A syntax error, since filters can't be written inside formulas
Row context extended across a relationship
A calculated column definition
Filter context, written directly into the formula
questions.explain: The Channel[ChannelName] = "Store" argument narrows down which rows count — that's filter context, set explicitly inside the formula via CALCULATE.

questions.q: Why can the exact same measure formula return different numbers on the same report?
options: Because the filter context surrounding it changes as slicers, filters, or visual selections change
This never happens — a measure's formula always returns the same number
Because Power BI caches an old value and doesn't always refresh it
Because measures recalculate randomly
questions.explain: A measure is re-evaluated within whatever filter context is currently active — the formula stays fixed, but the surrounding filters change what it calculates over.

questions.q: Why doesn't a calculated column's value change when a report's slicers change?
options: Because it was computed once, at refresh time, using only row context — it has no awareness of report-level filters
Because slicers only affect visuals, never the underlying data model
Because calculated columns are recalculated on every slicer change, just slower than measures
Because calculated columns can't be added to visuals at all
questions.explain: A calculated column only ever sees row context at the moment it's computed — it's stored, static data by the time any report filter gets applied.
